name: IP Protection (discontinued)
plain: A planned Chrome proxy to hide IP addresses from trackers. Discontinued per Oct 2025 announcement.
meaning: Would have routed third-party tracker traffic through two hops of proxies so a site saw a proxy IP, not the person's. The Apr 2025 plan targeted Incognito in Q3 2025. Status page now says Discontinue; the person's IP stays visible to sites.

web.api: Browser feature (no site API); site sees IP address of TCP peer

access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

safari.note: iCloud Private Relay is a separate OS service

data.metric: No data exposed by this feature

limits.headline: Can't hide your IP address from trackers in Chrome, since the plan was dropped
limits.user_action: Nothing. The feature was planned but never turned on
can: Have routed some traffic through a proxy to hide your address
Have kept your address from known trackers in Chrome
cannot: Run, since Chrome discontinued it in October 2025
Replace a VPN or private relay
Hide your address from the main site you visit

story.what_it_is: A plan by Chrome to hide your IP address from trackers. It was dropped.

marketing.name: IP Protection
marketing.pitch: Chrome pitched it as routing tracker traffic through proxies so sites would not see your real IP address.

story.for_you: You never got it in normal Chrome. Sites still see your real IP address. If you want one hidden, you need a VPN or a service like Private Relay.
story.for_makers: Chrome planned two proxy hops so a tracker would see a proxy address. It would have hurt ad fraud checks and country rules, and Google dropped it in 2025. Makers can still count on IP for location and abuse checks.

use_cases.example: An ad network keeps using IP to place you in a city, which a proxy would have blurred.
A bank would have seen only a proxy address, which makes its fraud and country checks harder.
A multiplayer game keeps banning cheaters by IP, which a proxy would have made harder.
A streaming site keeps blocking videos by country, which a proxy would have hidden.
A site keeps counting visits by region with no change.
A shop keeps showing local stock and prices from IP.

technical_bounds: Never became a default in regular Chrome
VPNs, iCloud Private Relay and Tor remain the real IP hiding options
Safari 27 beta blocks some tracker IP ranges instead (see related)

history.change: Plan to launch in Incognito Q3 2025 (Apr 22 2025 update)
